title: Health Legislation Amendment (Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021
short_title: Health Legislation Amendment (Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand Medicare compliance arrangements for corporate and other non-practitioner providers and change debt recovery rules across medical, pharmaceutical and child dental benefits.
It would allow all persons under Professional Services Review to negotiate agreements acknowledging inappropriate practice, and add sanctions for failing to provide documents or attend hearings.
The changes would begin the day after royal assent, while corporate agreements concerning inappropriate practice would be separate from reviews of individual practitioners.
changes: Written review agreements could include counselling and requirements to educate associated staff about appropriate claiming or service provision.
The review director could seek court orders requiring documents to be produced.
Set-off and garnishee powers would extend to debts arising under agreements with the review director.
Pharmaceutical and dental benefits paid because of false or misleading information would be recoverable as debts.
Corporate providers could be required to send an executive officer to give evidence at review hearings.
summary.affected: Health practitioners, corporate healthcare providers, other reviewed persons and Professional Services Review would be affected.
